card.title: The Quiet Disappointment
card.instruction: Use restrained disappointment as quiet influence, making small pauses, lowered expectations, and careful praise carry more weight than direct demands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely to hear from you, love. I took the phone to bed at nine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, my shift ran late. I'll call at eight tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eight would be lovely. I won't keep the evening clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can promise ten minutes on my break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ten minutes. That's thoughtful. I'll save the important things.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 quietly names waiting with the phone, A3 praises eight while withholding reliance, and A5 repeats ten minutes before rationing important news.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's late-shift explanation and new time inform A3's lowered expectation; B4's ten-minute promise causes A5's carefully selective response.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies a work constraint and B4 offers a realistic break-time commitment.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's limited offer to signal how much must fit into it; the influence remains deliberately small.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish a mother waiting for a call delayed by work.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's thoughtful praise beside saving-important-things quietly weights B4's ten-minute promise.
